n0001.title: GPT-3 and the Scaling Hypothesis
n0001.gist: GPT-3's unexpected meta-learning ability shows that simply scaling neural networks up produces intelligence-like behavior, vindicating the scaling hypothesis against a skeptical research establishment.

n0002.title: Introduction
n0002.gist: GPT-3 surprised researchers by learning to follow instructions and learn new tasks from examples, not just to generate text.

n0003.title: GPT-3 Overview
n0003.gist: GPT-3's scale-driven meta-learning marks a qualitative leap beyond GPT-2 and signals the arrival of the scaling hypothesis.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 learned to learn from examples purely through next-word prediction training at massive scale.

n0009.title: Flexing GPT
n0009.gist: Despite being a small, crude, obsolete architecture, GPT-3 still shows striking emergent capabilities that standard benchmarks fail to capture.

n0014.title: Scaling Evidence
n0014.gist: GPT-3's costly but continuing scaling curves show that bigger models keep paying off, contrary to fears of diminishing returns.

n0015.title: Baking The Cake
n0015.gist: GPT-3 is not full AGI, but its scaling shows unsupervised learning is becoming the foundational 'cake' beneath supervised and reinforcement learning.

n0023.title: Scaling
n0023.gist: Loss curves show GPT-3 is far from the point of diminishing returns, implying much further scaling remains fruitful.

n0032.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0032.gist: Across many domains, making models bigger and training them on more data reliably makes them more general and stable, and this pattern plausibly explains why scaling produces something like true understanding.

n0033.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0033.gist: Countless examples across deep learning show that scale alone induces generalization, stability, and meta-learning, likely because large models act as ensembles that favor simple, generalizable sub-models.

n0046.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0046.gist: The strong scaling hypothesis holds that sufficiently large, uniform neural networks will develop sophisticated behavior simply through scale, a claim once doubted but now vindicated.

n0050.title: Why Does Pretraining Work
n0050.gist: Language models improve from crude letter statistics to genuine reasoning as training deepens, and the pretraining thesis argues the final, hardest-won bits of prediction require real understanding, though this remains unproven in principle.

n0051.title: Pretraining Thesis
n0051.gist: Because human-generated text encodes logic, causality, and reasoning, a model that predicts it well must learn to understand these things.

n0056.title: Early Training Stages
n0056.gist: Early in training, models cheaply learn letter frequencies, spelling, and word boundaries before anything resembling meaning appears.

n0060.title: Later Training Stages
n0060.gist: As training continues, models progress from word associations to coherent sentences and finally to subtle, rare linguistic errors that require real understanding to fix.

n0066.title: The Deepest Bits
n0066.gist: The remaining gap to human-level prediction consists of the hardest cases—causality, theory of mind, and reasoning—implying that closing it requires genuine intelligence.

n0075.title: Reasons For Doubt
n0075.gist: The pretraining thesis is logically appealing but historically unproven, and only after GPT-3 did it become clear that raw scale, not a fundamentally new algorithm, sufficed.

n0086.title: Prospects And Critics
n0086.gist: Only OpenAI, driven by conviction in the scaling hypothesis, pursued this path aggressively, while other labs and expert critics doubted it and were repeatedly proven wrong.

n0087.title: Prospects
n0087.gist: Whether any organization will treat GPT-3 as a Sputnik moment and invest in scaling depends more on conviction than on available hardware.

n0100.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0100.gist: A decade of expert predictions against scaling and deep learning have been repeatedly falsified, exposing the authoritative 'voice' of AI skepticism as unfalsifiable and unaccountable.

n0116.title: Appendix: Agency In Models
n0116.gist: Because generative models trained on human data learn to imitate agents, agency is not a discrete or removable property but a useful, convergent capability that scale tends to produce even in seemingly non-agentic domains.

n0117.title: It From Byte
n0117.gist: Training on human-generated data inevitably teaches models to imitate agents, so agency emerges as a natural byproduct of scale.

n0126.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0126.gist: Since agency itself arises from non-agentic physical processes, no data can be strictly guaranteed free of latent agency.

n0130.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0130.gist: Treating natural systems as agents via variational reasoning is a powerful, general shortcut that neural networks are naturally inclined to adopt.

n0139.title: Inducing Emergent Agency
n0139.gist: Agency-like reasoning only emerges when a problem's scale and diversity make it cheaper than simpler alternatives, making its appearance an unpredictable empirical matter.

n0144.title: Turing Machines & Automata
n0144.gist: Even abstract systems like cellular automata and Turing machines can induce agent-like, intentional interpretations once meta-learning across many instances is required.

n0159.title: Ambient Agency
n0159.gist: Agency behaves like Turing-completeness: too useful and convergent a capability to reliably exclude from any sufficiently powerful, data-rich model.
